laterality: Five fixed paw identities: front image-left, outer image-left, short central rear, outer image-right, front image-right. Front and outer paws show three rounded dark toe tips each; the short central paw shows two tips and its root stays occluded. One central blue eye, four small teeth and a short flat-topped furry cylinder are retained without mirroring. Exact hidden leg-root depth remains a production hypothesis.

residualCaveats: Normal target/observed lift in pixels:01 24/53;02 20/56;03 16/12;04 20/43;05 24/37. The original targets remain recorded; the asymmetry and smaller projected central recovery are not claimed to be exact planned amplitudes.

Normal supporting sole differences are0..1px. Selected pixel support or recovery registration differences are generally within1px after whole-frame alignment; strict contact forces and continuous sliding are not established.

Same-normal128 projection versus pixel width/height deltas:01 +2/+1;02 +4/+1;03 +2/+3;04 0/0;05 +4/+1;06 0/-1. These residual contour differences did not show an unequivocal body/eye size jump in the static review.

Top fur is flatter on01/04 and more finely patterned on02/03/05/06. Eye reflections, dark pupil/mouth regions, teeth and fur line detail visibly change. In particular,06to01 changes from a grainier top to a smoother top.
The central paw retains only two visible toe tips and a concealed root; missing anatomy is not inferred or drawn in. Front/back root depth remains a production hypothesis.

Sequential recovery is readable, but strict forward displacement, body-center circulation and full biomechanical load transfer are not verified. Static review and exact APNG readback do not establish continuous perceived smoothness, collision behavior or real-game playback.
